div.head: Ger 17
div.ab: [17] Man sceal habban wængewædu, sulhgesidu, egeðgetigu ⁊ fela ðinga, ðe ic nu genæmnian ne can, ge eac mete, áwel ⁊ to odene fligel ⁊ andlamena fela: hwer, lead, cytel, hlædel, pannan, crocca, brandiren, dixas, stelmelas, cyfa, cyflas, cyrne, cysfæt, ceodan, wilian, windlas, systras, syfa, sædleap, hriddel, hersyfe, tæmespilan, fanna, trogas, æscena, hyfa, hunigbinna, beorbydene, bæðfæt, beodas, butas, bleda, melas, cuppan, seohhan, candelstafas, sealtfæt, sticfodder, piperhorn, cyste, mydercan, bearmteage, hlydan, sceamelas, stolas, læflas, leohtfæt, blacern, cyllan, sapbox, camb, yrsebinne, fodderhec, fyrgebeorh, meluhudern, ælhyde, ofnrace, mexscofle.

Man sceal habban wænge|wædu. Sulhgesidu . Egeðgetigu . 7 fela ðinga . ðe ic nu genæmnian ne can ge eac mete . awel . 7 to odene fligel . 7 and lamena fela . Hwer . lead . cytle . hlædel . pannan . crocca . brandiren . dixas stelmelas . cyfa . cyflas . cyrne . cysfæt . ceodan . wilian . windlas . Syf|tras . syfa . Sædleap . hriddel . hersyfe . tæ|mespilan , fanna . trogas. æscena. hyfa hunigbinna . beorbydene . bæðfæt . beodas . butas . bleda . melas . cuppan. seohhan . candelstafas. Sealtfæt. Sticfodder . Piperhorn . Cyste . mydercan . bearmteage . hlydan Scea|melas . Stolas . læflas . leohtfæt. blacern . cyllan . Sapbox. Camb . yrsebinne. fodder|hec . Fyregebeorh . meluhudern . ælhyde ofn|race . mexscofle .

Man sceal habban wængewædu, sulhgesidu, egeðgetigu, and fela ðinga ðe ic nu genæmnian ne can ge eac mete; awel and to odene fligel and andlamena fela: hwer, lead, cytel, hlædel, pannan, crocca, brandiren, dixas, stelmelas, cyfa, cyflas, cyrne, cysfæt, ceodan, wilian, windlas, systras, syfa, sædleap, hriddel, hersyfe, tæmespilan, fanna, trogas, æscena, hyfa hunigbinna, beorbydene, bæðfæt, beodas, butas, bleda, melas, cuppan, seohhan, candelstafas, sealtfæt, sticfodder, piperhorn, cyste, mydercan, bearmteage, hlydan, sceamelas, stolas, læflas, leohtfæt, blacern, cyllan, sapbox, camb, yrsebinne, fodderhec, fyrgebeorh, meluhudern, ælhyde, ofnrace, mexscofle.

Man muss haben: Wagenverdeck, Pflugzubehör, Eggengeräthe und viele Dinge, die ich jetzt nicht nennen kann, wie auch Maasse, Ahle und für die Tenne Dreschflegel und viele Geräthe: Kessel, Bleikessel, Kessel, Schöpfkelle, Pfanne, Topf, ‘Brandeisen’ [d. h. Feuerbock], Schüsseln, Henkelbecher, Eimer, Kübel, Butterkerne, Käsebehälter, Beutel [oder Körbe?], Weidenkörbe, Körbe, Sextar-Hohlmaasse, Siebe, Samenkorb, Sieb, Haarsieb, Siebstange, Futterschwinge, Tröge, Holzgefässe, Bienenkörbe, Honigkörbe, Bierbütten, Badewanne, Tische, Bütten [?], Schüsseln, Eimer, Becher, Seihen, Leuchter, Salzfass, Behälter aus Reisern [oder B. für Stöcke (= Pflöcke) oder für Löffel], Pfefferhornbüchse, Kiste, Koffer, Hefekiste, Stühle [? oder Deckel], Schemel, Stühle, Schüsseln, Lampe, Laterne [oder Leuchter], Flasche [oder Schlauch], Seifenbüchse, Kamm, Eisenkasten [?], Futterraufe, Feuerschutz [-schirm?], Mehlkammer, Aalbehälter [?], Ofengabel, Mistschaufel.

One must have: wagon-cover, plough-gear, harrowing-gear and many things that I cannot now name, as well as measures, an awl, and for the threshing-floor a flail, and many implements: cauldron, lead vessel, kettle, ladle, pan, pot, fire-dog, dishes, handled cups, pails, tubs, churn, cheese-vat, bags [or baskets?], willow baskets, baskets, sester-measures, sieves, seed-basket, riddle, hair-sieve, sieve-pole, winnowing-fan, troughs, ash-wood vessels, beehives, honey-bins, beer-barrels, bath-tub, tables, tubs[?], bowls, buckets, cups, strainers, candlesticks, salt-cellar, box for twigs [or for pegs, or for spoons], pepper-horn, chest, coffer, yeast-box, chairs[? or lids], stools, seats, bowls, lamp, lantern [or lamp-holder], flask [or leather bottle], soap-box, comb, iron bin[?], fodder-rack, fire-guard [-screen?], meal-store, eel-trap[?], oven-rake, dung-shovel.

One must have a wagon-cover, the appurtenances of a plough, apparatus belonging to a barrow, and many things which I cannot name or recount now: awl, and a flail for the threshing floor, and many clay loom-weights, pot, cauldron, kettle, ladle, pans, crockery, fire dog, pot with handles, tub, bucket, churn, cheese vat, bag, rolled-baskets, basket, pitchers, sieve, seed bucket, course sieve, hair sieve, sieve frame, winnowing fan, trough, ash-wood bucket, hive honey bin, beer-barrel, bathing tub, dishes, vessels, goblets, bowls, cups, sieve, candlesticks, salt cellar, spoon case, pepper horn, chest, money chest, yeast-box, seats, benches, stools, basins, soapbox, comb, manger, fodder-rack, meal-storehouse, eel-box?, oven rake, dung shovel.

One must have a wagon cover, the equipment for a plow, the equipment for a harrow, and many things which I cannot name now; also a measuring stick, awl, flail for the threshing floor, many loom weights, pot, cauldron, kettle, ladle, pans, crockery, firedog, dishes, pots with handles, tubs, buckets, churn, cheese vat, bags, rolled baskets, baskets, pitchers, sieves, seed bucket, coarse sieve, hair sieve, sieve frame, winnowing fans, troughs, ash-wood buckets, bucket to collect honey from the hive, beer barrel, bathtub, dishes, vessels, goblets, bowls, cups, sieve, candlesticks, saltcellar, spoon case, pepper horn, chest, money chest, yeast box, seats, benches, stools, basins, lantern, lamp, leather bottle, soapbox, comb, manger, fodder rack, fire screen, meal storehouse, eel-skin bag, oven rake, dung shovel.
div.note: B often drops ‘ge-’ (‘mete’ for ‘gemete’; compare Inscr.). After ‘cyfa’ follow five words beginning with c, then two with w, three with s, later five with b: perhaps the author used an alphabetical glossary. B's ‘butas’ is unclear (a or u). K: spacing and a missing comma corrected. Liebermann compares Gerefa 3, 11, 14, Rect 4.1, 5.1, 11 and 14.

folgen 5 Wörter mit c beginnend, dann 2 mit w, 3 mit s, später 5 mit b. Benutzte Verf. ein alphabetisches Glossar?
there follow 5 words beginning with c, then 2 with w, 3 with s, later 5 with b. Did the author use an alphabetical glossary?
a undeutlich wie n oder u
a indistinct, like n or u
Wohl zum Schutze der Ladung gegen Wetter, Herabfallen, Diebe
Probably to protect the load against weather, falling off and thieves
‘apparatus belonging to a harrow’ Toller Suppl.; vgl. o. 9.—Zu mete auf folg. Z. vgl. Abfall des ge- in scadwis 1
‘apparatus belonging to a harrow’ Toller Suppl.; cf. above 9.—On mete in the next line cf. the loss of ge- in scadwis 1
see above 12; below 17 f.

‘Dreizack’ nach Glosse fuscinula, tridens Holthausen in Beibl. zu Anglia Nov. 1909, 328. Nach jenen weist Glossen [h]arpago, uncus nach Toller Suppl. 57. Gegen diesen ist dann æl : subula davon zu trennen

‘trident’, according to the gloss fuscinula, tridens, Holthausen in Beibl. zu Anglia Nov. 1909, 328. In addition to those, Toller Suppl. 57 attests the glosses [h]arpago, uncus. Against him, æl : subula must then be kept separate from this
vgl. 14
cf. 14

‘Blei’ (Kluge, Toller) passt nicht; gegen Verbindung leadcytel spricht der Punkt dazwischen; ‘kitchen copper’ Sweet; diese Bed. ist Mengl. und neuengl. nachgewiesen; Mätzner s. v. led, Stratmann, Mayhew, Halliwell, Bateson Rec. of Leicester I 219. Bleikessel dienen für abzurahmende Milch (Hardy [o. Rect 16²] 250), zum Brauen (‘plumbum, a copper anciently called a lead, used in the brewhouse’; Gray Priory of St. Radegund 183), zum Baden (Hale Dom. of St. Pauls lxxxiij. xcvij), Salzsieden (Ellis Introd. to Dom. I 128), Ordal des Kesselfangs; s. d. Gl 6. ‘Bleigefäss, kleinen Kessel’ Sk-Wi, wo für pa., cr. nur ‘Brotkrog’ [?]

‘lead’ (Kluge, Toller) does not fit; the point between them tells against the combination leadcytel; ‘kitchen copper’ Sweet; this meaning is attested in ME and Mod. Engl.; Mätzner s. v. led, Stratmann, Mayhew, Halliwell, Bateson Rec. of Leicester I 219. Lead cauldrons serve for milk that is to be skimmed (Hardy [above Rect 16²] 250), for brewing (‘plumbum, a copper anciently called a lead, used in the brewhouse’; Gray Priory of St. Radegund 183), for bathing (Hale Dom. of St. Pauls lxxxiij. xcvij), for salt-boiling (Ellis Introd. to Dom. I 128), and for the ordeal of the cauldron; see that word in Gl 6. ‘lead vessel, small cauldron’ Sk-Wi, where for pa., cr. only ‘bread-crock’ [?]
Nicht ‘Brenneisen’ (Kluge). ‘Firedog, grate’ Sweet, ‘andiron, trivet’ Toller Suppl., andera, tripes Ælfric, ‘Dreifuss, Rost’ Mätzner, Stratmann
Not ‘branding-iron’ (Kluge). ‘Firedog, grate’ Sweet, ‘andiron, trivet’ Toller Suppl., andera, tripes Ælfric, ‘tripod, gridiron’ Mätzner, Stratmann
So Kluge; ‘vessel with a stem or handle’ Toller, Sweet, Sk-Wi
So Kluge; ‘vessel with a stem or handle’ Toller, Sweet, Sk-Wi

Ahd. kubil Kluge; Toller Suppl. setzt cyf [dolium], cyfel mit neuengl. keeve, cowl [Bottich, Zuber] identisch.—Statt ‘Käsebehälter’ nächster Zeile bessere ‘Käsefass, in dem man saure Milch zu Käse presst’

OHG kubil Kluge; Toller Suppl. takes cyf [dolium], cyfel to be identical with Mod. Engl. keeve, cowl [vat, tub].—For ‘Käsebehälter’ in the next line read ‘Käsefass, in dem man saure Milch zu Käse presst’
‘ceode Korb’? Kluge; ‘Säcke’ Sk-Wi; ‘Geldbeutel’ Ritter (o. 12³) CXIX 177; ‘bag, pouch’ laut Glosse marsupia Sweet, Toller Suppl.
‘ceode basket’? Kluge; ‘sacks’ Sk-Wi; ‘purse’ Ritter (above 12³) CXIX 177; ‘bag, pouch’, according to the gloss marsupia, Sweet, Toller Suppl.
vgl. Rect. 4, 1. 5, 1
cf. Rect. 4, 1. 5, 1
vgl. ebd. 11
cf. ibid. 11
Mittel- und neuenglisch; Stratmann, Mätzner, Halliwell
Middle and Modern English; Stratmann, Mätzner, Halliwell

‘stake to support sieve’ Sweet; Mengl. temsynge staff : lignum quod portat cribrum Toller, pil ‘stake’ ansetzend. Fehlt Sk-Wi.—Zur folg. Zeile vgl. Toller Suppl. s. v. æscen; ‘Aschenfass’ [falsch] Sk-Wi
‘stake to support sieve’ Sweet; ME temsynge staff : lignum quod portat cribrum Toller, positing pil ‘stake’. Not in Sk-Wi.—On the following line cf. Toller Suppl. s. v. æscen; ‘ash-tub’ [wrong] Sk-Wi
vgl. ebd. 5
cf. ibid. 5
vgl. Rect. 16. Oder Näpfe
cf. Rect. 16. Or bowls
So Kluge, Sweet; ‘dishes or tables’ Toller Suppl. 79; beod : urna Napier Glossaries n. 1838; ‘Becken’ Sk-Wi, wo 7 folg. Wörter fehlen
So Kluge, Sweet; ‘dishes or tables’ Toller Suppl. 79; beod : urna Napier Glossaries n. 1838; ‘basins’ Sk-Wi, where the 7 following words are missing
Nebenformen zu bytt (?): ‘Schlauch’ (Kluge), ‘Fass’ (Sweet), ‘Bütte’ (Bo.-Toller). Toller Suppl. 110 emendiert bucas ‘Gefässe’.—Zu cuppan vgl. Toller Suppl.: cuppe
By-forms of bytt (?): ‘leather bottle’ (Kluge), ‘cask’ (Sweet), ‘tub’ (Bo.-Toller). Toller Suppl. 110 emends to bucas ‘vessels’.—On cuppan cf. Toller Suppl.: cuppe
blede Rect. 14 übersetzt Quadr. cuppam
blede in Rect. 14 is translated by Quadr. as cuppam
blede Rect. 14 übersetzt Quadr. cuppam
blede in Rect. 14 is translated by Quadr. as cuppam

‘Futteral, Ständer für Stöcke’ Kluge; ‘case for spoons’ Sweet, Sk-Wi; oder ‘pegs’ oder ‘made of twigs’ Toller; vgl. Angelsächs. Kisten aus Ruten oder Stäben bei Heyne Deut. Wohnung 115.—Zum zweitfolg. Worte s. Toller Suppl.: cist

‘case, stand for sticks’ Kluge; ‘case for spoons’ Sweet, Sk-Wi; or ‘pegs’ or ‘made of twigs’ Toller; cf. Anglo-Saxon chests made of rods or staves in Heyne Deut. Wohnung 115.—On the next word but one see Toller Suppl.: cist
Über Verwendung der Hefe bei Agsa. s. Cockayne Leechdoms III 355
On the use of yeast among the Anglo-Saxons see Cockayne Leechdoms III 355
‘hlyde = Deckel?’ Kluge; aber vielleicht für hleda : sedile [Sitz] Ælfric; ‘Sitzbänke, Fussbänke’ Sk-Wi
‘hlyde = lid?’ Kluge; but perhaps for hleda : sedile [seat] Ælfric; ‘benches, footstools’ Sk-Wi
læfel ‘Schüssel’ Kluge; glossiert cyphus, vas, (aqua)manile ‘cup, vessel, bowl’ Sweet, Toller; ‘Waschbecken’ Sk-Wi
læfel ‘dish’ Kluge; glosses cyphus, vas, (aqua)manile ‘cup, vessel, bowl’ Sweet, Toller; ‘wash-basin’ Sk-Wi

Glossiert uter [‘Lederschläuche’ Sk-Wi], ascopera [Lederränzel], culeus Bo.-Toller, und Suppl. s. v. cyll; hier zitiert er unsere Stelle unter cille ‘Lampe, Feuerschale’, was zu den zwei vorhergebenden Begriffen viel besser passt

Glosses uter [‘leather bottles’ Sk-Wi], ascopera [leather pouch], culeus Bo.-Toller, and Suppl. s. v. cyll; there he cites our passage under cille ‘lamp, fire-pan’, which fits much better with the two preceding terms
So Kluge; sopere ‘Seifenmacher’ ist im 12. Jh. festes Gewerbe; Bateson Rec. of Leicester 14; dagegen ‘resin [oder ‘soap-’ Sk-Wi] box’ Sweet, Toller
So Kluge; sopere ‘soap-maker’ is an established trade in the 12th cent.; Bateson Rec. of Leicester 14; on the other hand ‘resin [or ‘soap-’ Sk-Wi] box’ Sweet, Toller

so Sk-Wi; s. irsenhelm ‘Eisenhelm’; ‘kind of (iron) box’ Sweet (Toller); ‘Drahtkrippe, zu isern?’ Kluge [binn : præsepe]; das passt gut zum folgenden. Hyrsebinn ‘Pferdekrippe’ empfiehlt Schlutter Engl. Stud. 42 (1910) 203; ryselbinne ‘Fettkasten’ Ritter o. 17⁸. Vielleicht ist Metathese von rysc, also ‘Binsenkorb’ anzunehmen

so Sk-Wi; see irsenhelm ‘iron helmet’; ‘kind of (iron) box’ Sweet (Toller); ‘wire crib, from isern?’ Kluge [binn : præsepe]; this fits well with what follows. Schlutter Engl. Stud. 42 (1910) 203 recommends Hyrsebinn ‘horse-manger’; ryselbinne ‘fat-box’ Ritter above 17⁸. Perhaps a metathesis of rysc, and so ‘rush basket’, should be assumed
‘fodderrack’ Sweet; hec jetzt hatch, mengl.: hacche; Mätzner
‘fodderrack’ Sweet; hec now hatch, ME hacche; Mätzner
‘firescreen’? Sweet; ‘-gitter’ Sk-Wi. Wohl Vorrichtung gegen Feuersgefahr. Für ‘Kamin’ kommt fyrhus vor; Heyne Wohnung 120
‘firescreen’? Sweet; ‘-grating’ Sk-Wi. Probably a device against the danger of fire. For ‘fireplace’ fyrhus occurs; Heyne Wohnung 120
‘Mehllager’ Kluge, ‘mealstorehouse’ Sweet, wohl synonym mit meluhus : farinale bei Toller
‘meal-store’ Kluge, ‘mealstorehouse’ Sweet, probably synonymous with meluhus : farinale in Toller
‘eel-receptacle?’ Sweet; dagegen ‘eel-skin’ Toller Suppl.; vgl. Ine 70, 1². ‘Ölflasche’ Sk-Wi [falsch]
‘eel-receptacle?’ Sweet; on the other hand ‘eel-skin’ Toller Suppl.; cf. Ine 70, 1². ‘oil-flask’ Sk-Wi [wrong]
‘ovenrake [‘-kratzer’ Sk-Wi]’ Sweet; glossiert rotabulum [Schürholz] Toller
‘ovenrake [‘-scraper’ Sk-Wi]’ Sweet; glosses rotabulum [poker] Toller
